3.title: iPhone, Android and other personal devices

rejected.reason: Reading the Mac mini's screen sounds safe, but it cannot report a stuck Messages app because the question itself arrives through Messages, and each screenshot would send both parents' message threads to a cloud model.
A schedule card in the Mac app's floating panel cannot be triggered from iMessage or from a scheduled job, and no Mac in the house is a screen the family looks at.
Tidying a Downloads folder is better done by a weekly scheduled script with no agent at all; the agent route needs shell access on a parent's laptop.
A shared folder on a parent's Mac adds a new trust surface for something an iMessage attachment already does, and files are capped at 16 MiB.
Full screen control of a parent's everyday laptop puts private data, an untrusted screen and every way out into one tool with no per-action confirmation.

Fetching documents from a signed-in portal would give a shared agent an account, and every expired session means signing in again by hand at the Mac, which is slower than downloading the file on a phone.
Knowing which Mac was used last answers no real family question, and the Logbook plugin behind the fuller version is continuous screen capture sent to a cloud model.
Find My, Maps arrival sharing and Check In already answer where the other parent is, without Always-on location and a gateway console on both personal phones.
The Health app already shows today's steps and sleep; Happy's version needs the gateway app on the phone, sends health figures to a cloud model and cuts sleep off at midnight.
A spare iPhone as a kitchen talk device cannot be limited to one agent or to the adults, and even its talk-only pairing lets whoever picks it up read every conversation.
Driving a spare iPhone through iPhone Mirroring means letting an agent control Happy's whole Mac desktop, right next to Messages, and the phone would have to share Happy's Apple Account.

A SIM in a spare iPhone for ordinary text messages costs a monthly line, puts a second device on Happy's Apple Account and serves nobody, since both parents use iMessage and the school texts their own numbers.
Developer automation over a cable can tap any app, but it needs Xcode, Developer Mode, weekly re-signing and an agent holding everything at once; it is a testing tool, not a family feature.
Reading two-factor codes, opening banking apps and leaving a phone unlocked and unattended stay on the never list, with the text-message commands denied in config.
An always-listening microphone on the Mac mini would install the Mac app on the machine that holds every secret, cannot tell who is speaking, and would send the children's speech to a cloud model.
This is the same kitchen phone as IPH-06 seen from the voice side: no pairing keeps it inside one agent, and its voice settings need administrator access that the talk-only pairing does not have.
A phone number for Happy needs a public web address, which the Tailscale-only design rules out, and the phones already deliver emergency alerts on their own.
Happy phoning a business in a synthetic voice breaks the family-only and no-bookings rules; a four-line call script that the parent uses is the safe version and needs nothing new.
FaceTime Audio with Happy cannot run without weakening System Integrity Protection and adding an administrator account and Xcode to the gateway Mac, all against the M0 baseline.
A meeting note-taker needs a browser on the gateway Mac and puts other people's speech, including a teacher's words about a child, into a cloud model, for a handful of meetings a year.
Find My already sends a recurring arrive or leave notice; Happy's version would switch on gateway web hooks whose single shared secret would sit on each phone.
Pulling a parent's position from their phone on demand works, but Find My answers the same question without passing the location through a cloud model or keeping it in chat history.
This is the same Health summary as IPH-05 from the home lens: a scheduled pull usually finds the app asleep, so the line in the evening brief would often be missing.
A wall tablet showing a Happy dashboard would need gateway read access that also opens both parents' conversations; a shared calendar app or the printed week sheet does the job.
Locks, the garage door, the alarm, the gate and room cameras stay on the never list, and any future home hub must leave them unexposed and blocked in code.

A logged-in portal reader would hold a parent's account, read untrusted pages and have a way out all at once, and every expired session needs the operator at the Mac mini; the portal's own emails and app do better.
Letting Happy drive a parent's real signed-in Chrome hands an agent that person's whole logged-in life.

Filling in a camp registration form in a browser would combine a child's details, an arbitrary web page and a booking; a registration-day card with the link, the answers to paste and a reminder is the safe substitute, built from existing features.
The bill-due line already exists in F060 and autopay covers most of it, and a usage analysis would need a parent to download a data file from the very portal that already shows the numbers.
Saving a web page as a PDF takes two taps on a phone, printing included; the agent version needs new plumbing between the web-reading agent and the printer.
A store stock check usually ends in 'could not verify' because retailer sites block automation, and the retailer's own app is faster and more accurate.
Stealth proxies, hosted browsers and CAPTCHA solving stay off; Happy reports the block instead of working round it.
A pinned session goal disappears at the nightly reset and has no status view on iMessage; saying the goal in plain words does as much.

Automatic self-learning, where Happy rewrites its own skills in the background, is on by default and should be switched off in config; new routines arrive only through operator-reviewed skills (AUT-06).
OpenClaw's task board and drawn widgets live only in the Control UI and cannot appear in an iMessage thread; a shared Reminders list already does the family job.
Model-written code and large sub-agent fan-out have no place in a family agent and stay off, together with script triggers.
A heartbeat that wakes the agent every 30 minutes to 'notice things' stays off; each recurring need is its own named job.
Nightly automatic memory consolidation is one switch for the whole gateway, so it stays off and memories are promoted by hand in the weekly review.
A screen journal that screenshots a Mac every 30 seconds and sends the frames to a cloud model is surveillance, not a family feature.
Cloud workers, external coding harnesses, session sharing, team reports and Vault are built for development teams and do not fit a one-Mac family agent.
A real phone number for texting or calling Happy needs a paid provider and a public web address, or weakened Mac security for FaceTime; none of that fits this house.
1Password as an agent tool would show household secrets to a cloud model, and the Keychain chosen in M0 already covers the gateway's own keys.
Generated songs, video clips, memes and GIFs each need another cloud provider or a wrapper and solve no household problem; nano-pdf is a slide editor, not a form filler.
A parent's phone location and daily Health summary both work in principle, but Family Sharing and the Health app already show them with no cloud model in the path.

A Skylight-style kitchen board would mean pairing a shared-room tablet as a gateway console that can open both parents' private conversations; a shared calendar on an old iPad or the printed sheet does the job.
For 'is Jordan nearly home' and arrival alerts, Happy should point to Find My instead of collecting coordinates.
For the kids' homework help today, a product built for under-13s such as Khanmigo is the better choice until Happy has a local model.
Calling Happy, wake-up calls and calls to businesses need either a public web address or weakened Mac security, so calls stay off.
Reservations, orders and repair bookings are on the never list; Happy stops one step earlier and hands the parent a ready-to-tap result.
Thread summaries and reply drafts are now built into Gmail itself, so Happy's personal-inbox drafting features rank below the school mailbox.
The USPS Informed Delivery digest already reaches the phone and is mostly pictures of envelopes, which Happy's mail reader cannot see.
A weekly fuel price line gives regional averages only, while map apps already show prices at each station.
No Windows or Linux PC is in the house, and the route to operate one is rougher than the Mac route with the same risks.
Happy should not hold the router's admin login; pausing a device and filtering the kids' DNS are one-time settings in the router's own app.
Car status and remote commands need a registered developer application and a publicly hosted key, and the main commands are locks and openings, which the never list bans.
Image generation works, but it needs OpenAI's catalog provider, which changes how voice memos and PDFs are routed and has no storage switch; too many side effects for coloring pages.
Leave-by nudges duplicate the time-to-leave alerts the phone's calendar already sends.
A needs-reply tracker duplicates the nudges Gmail already shows at the top of the inbox.
Package tracking from carrier emails duplicates the carrier apps, USPS Informed Delivery and Gmail's own package tracking.
Lobster's approve-to-continue pipelines amount to host shell access inside a person's agent, and the existing approval hook already provides the gate.

findings.text: Controlling a computer: possible on paper, not safely on this Mac today. OpenClaw's computer tool can drive a Mac only through the separate OpenClaw.app, which is not installed. Once that app is paired and has its macOS permissions, the grant is durable: no per-action confirmation, no lease or expiry, no limit to one app, and it works only on an unlocked desktop. The only unlocked desktop on the Mac mini is Happy's own, with Messages signed in, so one tool would hold the family's chats, an untrusted screen and a way to send. Pairing the Mac app also brings shell execution and desktop sharing. Decision: write the deny list now (MAC-04, wave A), offer fixed allowlisted Mac actions and printing instead (F078, F080, wave C), and keep the clean-VM pilot (MAC-03, MAC-01, MAC-02, MAC-15, MAC-05, MAC-07) as 'later'. It is not in wave D because the Mac app inside the VM would itself be a signed-in gateway console that the agent could click on.

The model vendors give the same advice. Anthropic's own guidance for computer use is a dedicated virtual machine with minimal privileges, no account logins, an allowlist of sites and a person confirming anything with real-world consequences, and it warns that text on the screen can override instructions. The benchmark that started this field (OSWorld, 369 tasks) reported people completing about 72% and the best model about 12% in 2024. Newer scores are much higher but vendor-reported, so the only number that should decide anything is the acceptance test on the family's own chores (MAC-05).

Controlling a connected idle iPhone: no. OpenClaw's iPhone app is a sensor and chat client with a fixed command list (camera, location, calendar and reminders reads, notifications); its own page says it is not a computer-use backend, and camera and screen commands need the app open in the foreground. The only way to tap inside other apps is Apple's iPhone Mirroring driven by the Mac computer tool. That needs the phone signed in to the same Apple Account as the Mac user (Happy's), iOS 18 or later, locked and near the Mac, and it inherits every problem in the first finding, so IPH-08 is not recommended. Cable-based developer automation (IPH-12) and Apple's accessibility features (IPH-13) do not give a usable route either.

What a spare iPhone could still do is small: one still photo on request from a window sill (IPH-02, experimental, the app must stay on screen) or a read-only bridge to Apple Calendar and Reminders (IPH-04). The kitchen voice terminal (IPH-06, VOX-10) and the SMS bridge (IPH-11) are not recommended. Whatever its role, a phone running the app holds a gateway credential: even the talk-only pairing keeps read access to every session, and the installed docs show no way to pin a device or a wake word to one agent.

If an idle phone that Happy can operate is ever wanted, it is an Android phone, not an iPhone. Android is the only platform whose command list includes reading the screen and tapping, and the only one that forwards other apps' notifications. It stays 'later' (IPH-14, IPH-15): the family owns no Android phone, the installed Android page never mentions the Accessibility Control switch the feature depends on, the tool is owner-only so only Tony's requests could use it, and a forwarded notification arrives as a trusted system event in whatever session the phone names.

Every phone that runs the OpenClaw app is a control console for the whole gateway, not a per-person chat window. The default pairing hands over admin, approvals, read and write; 'limited' removes only admin; and the docs state that read access is not a per-person privacy boundary. So the app's real benefits (tap-to-approve cards, push alerts, native chat with files, live voice) fit Tony's phone only. That is wave D: pair Tony's iPhone (IPH-01, OCL-01), then try Talk on it behind the voice guardrails (VOX-03, VOX-01). Jordan stays on iMessage until OpenClaw can confine a phone to one person.

Voice and calls: the best hands-free path already exists and costs nothing. Siri sends and reads iMessages, so Happy only needs a short 'driving' reply style (VOX-06, wave A). A phone number for Happy and calls to third parties are not recommended: the calling plugin needs a public web address, which the Tailscale-only design excludes, and FaceTime calling needs reduced System Integrity Protection, an administrator account and Xcode on the gateway Mac.

The house: OpenClaw has no Home Assistant or HomeKit integration of its own. Hue and Sonos are reachable through small host-side plugins around the openhue and sonoscli tools (F076, F077, wave C, with HOM-02 as the record of how each tool signs in), and the LG TV through an allowlisted Shortcut (HOM-11). Home Assistant's MCP server is the later single-hub route (HOM-01): it is limited to the entities a parent exposes and to administrator accounts by default, and it hands out the tools of Home Assistant's own assistant interface, not one tool per device. The never list (locks, garage, alarm, gate, cameras; HOM-12) therefore has to be enforced by what is exposed in Home Assistant and by a code hook.

Several safety assumptions in the 9 Oct plan need tightening before anything new ships. Only the before_tool_call and before_agent_run hooks block when their code fails; message_sending and reply_payload_sending are logged and skipped, so the family-only recipient pin, the kill switch and the lost-phone lock must sit on the first kind (G009, G005, CRT-02). Scheduled jobs can deliver to a webhook, and script triggers run with the owning agent's full tool policy, so cron.triggers.enabled goes to false before any agent gets the scheduling tool (AUT-08, F007, AUT-01). Background self-learning defaults to auto and should be set to off (AUT-07). The node command deny list goes in before any device is paired (MAC-04, HOM-08).

store:false protects less than the 9 Oct plan implies. OpenAI's data-controls page says the setting governs stored application state only; abuse-monitoring logs, which can contain prompts and responses, are kept for up to 30 days unless the organisation is approved for Zero Data Retention. That covers family photos and PDFs (F001, F002, F064) and any realtime voice (VOX-02), and it becomes a new decision for Tony.

Most of the new family value is not 'advanced' at all. Official, free feeds become watch jobs that need no model call: product, food and vehicle recalls (SRC-03, SRC-04, SRC-05), team schedule changes (SRC-09), and school platforms set to email one digest to the school mailbox (SRC-08, MKT-01). The critic pass added trust and recovery items nothing else covered: lock out a lost phone (CRT-02), an honest reply when the model is down (CRT-04), a recovery card for Jordan (CRT-05), a shared what-was-given log on sick days (CRT-10) and a childcare coverage planner (CRT-11).

A local yes/no classifier is closer than the 9 Oct notes said. The @openclaw/onnx plugin is published on npm in a 2026.9.7 build that accepts this gateway version, so the privacy gate (F084) and the urgent-mail gate (F055) can try an on-device classifier in wave B without the skipped local-model milestone. It is unproven on this Mac, so it is labelled experimental (OCL-14).

new_decisions.question: Install OpenClaw.app (the Mac menu-bar app) anywhere at all?
new_decisions.options: (a) No: keep the Homebrew gateway only and deny computer.act, desktop.stream and the other node host commands in config. (b) Later, only inside a clean macOS virtual machine for an attended pilot. (c) On Happy's own desktop on the Mac mini.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a) for this batch. Option (c) should never happen, because Messages is signed in on that desktop. Revisit (b) only when the app inside the VM no longer has to be a signed-in gateway console, or after M6.

new_decisions.question: Pair Tony's own iPhone with the OpenClaw app, knowing it becomes a second control console for the whole gateway?
new_decisions.options: (a) Tony's phone only, after the node deny list is in place. (b) Both parents' phones. (c) No phones.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a) as wave D. Not (b): even a limited pairing can read and write across both parents' agents, so Jordan stays on iMessage until OpenClaw can confine a phone to one person.

new_decisions.question: Dedicate a spare phone to Happy, and if so which kind and under which account?
new_decisions.options: (a) No spare phone for now. (b) A spare iPhone under its own Apple Account, locked to the OpenClaw app with Guided Access, as a still-camera only. (c) A cheap Android phone on its own Google account for school and team app notifications.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a) now. An iPhone cannot be operated as a computer, and its remaining roles are fragile. Consider (c) only after two school weeks of the school digest show a gap that only an app can fill, and test the Accessibility Control switch on a real device before buying. Never sign a spare phone in to a parent's Apple Account.

new_decisions.question: Add a telephony provider (a phone number for Happy) or any public web address for the gateway?
new_decisions.options: (a) No. (b) A Twilio or Telnyx number for family-only outbound alert calls. (c) Full call-in and SMS.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a). Every calling and SMS route needs a public endpoint that the Tailscale-only design excludes, and the phones already deliver emergency alerts.

new_decisions.question: Switch on the gateway's HTTP hooks so that phone Shortcuts (arrive home, CarPlay, an NFC tag) can nudge Happy?
new_decisions.options: (a) Keep hooks off. (b) On, with one fixed mapping per event and a tool-less target agent.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a) for this batch: the hook secret is one shared string that cannot be a secret reference, it would live inside a phone shortcut, and it also opens the free-text wake and agent endpoints.

new_decisions.question: Home devices: separate small plugins per brand, or Home Assistant as the single hub?
new_decisions.options: (a) Direct plugins for Hue and Sonos now, Home Assistant when its virtual machine is built for the kids' speaker (M5). (b) Home Assistant first. (c) Both at once.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a). Not (c): two paths to the same lights double the places a never-list rule has to be enforced.

new_decisions.question: Voice: which speech engines, and is realtime voice with a separate OpenAI key acceptable?
new_decisions.options: (a) Local speech only: a local neural voice on the Mac mini, the keyless Microsoft online voice switched off, native turn-by-turn Talk on Tony's phone. (b) Add an OpenAI Platform key for realtime voice.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a). Realtime voice sits outside the per-person store-off providers and its spoken confirmation is not tied to a speaker; treat (b) as a later experiment.

new_decisions.question: Ask OpenAI for Zero Data Retention (or Modified Abuse Monitoring) before photos, PDFs and medical bills go to the cloud model?
new_decisions.options: (a) Apply and wait for approval before turning attachments on. (b) Turn attachments on under store:false and accept up to 30 days of abuse-monitoring logs. (c) Keep attachments off.
new_decisions.recommendation: Apply now; if approval is slow, (b) with the document privacy gate (F084) in front, and keep medical bills (F064) for after approval. This refines decision 3 of 9 Oct.

new_decisions.question: Let the person agents read skill files, and who may ask for a new routine?
new_decisions.options: (a) Allow the read tool for skills only, Tony reviews every skill before deploy, background self-learning set to off. (b) No skills; keep routines in AGENTS.md.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a). Set skills.workshop.autonomous.mode to off in the same change, since the default is auto.

new_decisions.question: When the main model fails, may the smaller sibling model answer?
new_decisions.options: (a) Yes: one same-vendor fallback on each parent's agent, plus a plain 'the model is down' line. (b) No fallback: an honest failure line only.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a) for the parents' agents. Rebuild the bin and weather reminders as command jobs so they do not depend on any model.

new_decisions.question: What can Jordan do alone when Happy is down or a phone is lost?
new_decisions.options: (a) A printed recovery card, the pause phrase, a lock-one-person-out phrase, and a sealed envelope with the non-admin happy password. (b) The same plus an administrator credential. (c) Nothing; wait for Tony.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a), and rehearse a power-cut restart once. Add the administrator credential only if the rehearsal shows the happy password cannot unlock the disk.

new_decisions.question: May anyone beyond the two parents (a grandparent, a regular sitter) text Happy?
new_decisions.options: (a) No. (b) Yes, a guest tier that answers only from a fixed card.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a) for now: an allowlisted guest could also send slash commands, and an approval hook cannot tell who answered. Keep the sitter sheet (F036) as something a parent forwards.

new_decisions.question: Try the local ONNX classifier plugin on this gateway?
new_decisions.options: (a) Install the 2026.9.7 build of the plugin and test it on a small labelled set in wave B. (b) Wait for a later OpenClaw upgrade. (c) Stay with keyword rules.
new_decisions.recommendation: (a). It needs no gateway upgrade, and a measured classifier makes the privacy gate and the urgent-school-mail gate stronger without any cloud call.

contradictions.what: Whether a 'limited' or 'voice-node' pairing keeps a phone inside one person's agent. IPH-07, HOM-08 and VOX-03 (and the 11 Oct section of the catalog) treat limited pairing as the safe choice for Jordan's phone or a spare phone; the reviewers say such a phone is still a gateway-wide client.
contradictions.resolution: The installed docs support the reviewers: --limited removes only operator.admin (write, approvals and read remain), --voice-node keeps operator.read, and operator.read is stated not to be a per-person privacy boundary. App pairing is Tony-only for now.

contradictions.what: How many approvals pairing takes. IPH-01 says two (the device, then its command surface) and MAC-04 counts that as a separate gate; the reviewers say a setup code approves both in one step.
contradictions.resolution: The installed docs support the reviewers: SSH-verified pairing and node-profile setup codes approve the initial command surface; only later expansions need a fresh approval. The deny list, not the approval step, is the dependable gate.

contradictions.what: Whether the local ONNX classifier plugin can be installed on 2026.9.7. OCL-14 was filed as blocked (needs 2026.10.1) and the 9 Oct catalog calls onnx unpublished; the reviewer says a matching build exists.
contradictions.resolution: The npm registry lists @openclaw/onnx 2026.9.7 with a peer requirement of openclaw 2026.9.7 or later, so the reviewer is right: no upgrade is needed and the feature is experimental, not blocked.

contradictions.what: Whether a wake word can be routed to a named agent. IPH-06, VOX-10 and MKT-08 rely on it; the iPhone and voice reviewers found no way to set such a route.
contradictions.resolution: The installed page describes the routing format (a route can target an agent id) but lists only a read method, voicewake.routing.get, with no set method or editor. The reviewers' reading stands: the kitchen-terminal design cannot be configured as written.

contradictions.what: The same spare-iPhone kitchen terminal was judged three ways: IPH-06 rejected by its feasibility reviewer and blocked by its security reviewer, VOX-10 left as experimental by the voice feasibility reviewer and blocked by the voice security reviewer.
contradictions.resolution: The facts behind the rejection are in the installed docs: the voice-node credential still carries operator.read, and operator.read includes session reads. Both ids go to the not-recommended list until speech is local and a device can be confined to one agent.

contradictions.what: IPH-05 and HOM-09 propose the phone Health summary as something to build; OCL-16 files the same command as not recommended.
contradictions.resolution: The facts agree (health.summary exists behind an explicit allow entry); only the judgement differs. The reviewers of IPH-05 and HOM-09 lowered both to experimental with value 1, so all three are listed as not recommended.

contradictions.what: OCL-07 proposes switching on nightly Dreaming for the two private agents; AUT-13 and the roadmap keep it off.
contradictions.resolution: The roadmap keeps dreaming off from M0 and both reviewers describe it as one gateway-wide switch, so the keep-off position stands; the recall half survives as AUT-14.

contradictions.what: SRC-02 was filed as not recommended because no free pollen feed covers the United States; its reviewer says Google's Pollen API is free at this volume.
contradictions.resolution: Google's price list shows 5,000 free Pollen events a month, so the reviewer is right. It still needs a billing-enabled Google Cloud project, so it is folded into the morning brief (F013) as an optional line.

contradictions.what: Whether the released Android app can be operated. The 11 Oct section of the catalog and IPH-14 describe screen control as available once Accessibility Control is on; the feasibility reviewer found nothing showing the released app has that switch.
contradictions.resolution: Both are partly right. The command-policy page says Android advertises the mobile UI commands only while Accessibility Control is enabled, but the installed Android app page lists its command families without them and never mentions that setting. Treat it as unconfirmed until tested on a real device.

contradictions.what: IPH-15 describes a forwarded Android notification as a wrapped turn for a tool-less reader agent; both reviewers say it arrives as a system event.
contradictions.resolution: The installed source supports the reviewers: the gateway turns the notification into a system event on the session key the phone supplies, or on the system main session when none is given. The reader and the delivery step are in-house work that does not exist yet.

contradictions.what: The 9 Oct catalog treats store:false as the condition that makes sending family photos and PDFs to OpenAI acceptable (decision 3); the sourcing file for F001 says the setting covers less.
contradictions.resolution: OpenAI's data-controls page supports the sourcing file: abuse-monitoring logs, which can include prompts and responses, are kept up to 30 days by default whatever store says, unless Zero Data Retention is approved.

contradictions.what: The 9 Oct catalog uses message_sending as a second gate for the family delivery pin (G009) and reply_payload_sending for the notification policy (G001); the sourcing files say those hooks do not fail closed.
contradictions.resolution: The hook reference supports the sourcing files: before_tool_call and before_agent_run block on an error or timeout, while message_sending and reply_payload_sending are logged and skipped. Recipient limits belong on before_tool_call; quiet hours and caps built on the other hooks are best effort.

contradictions.what: The roadmap's never list and the 9 Oct catalog say provider terms are 13+; the sourcing file for F072 could not confirm that wording.
contradictions.resolution: Not resolved. OpenAI's terms page returned HTTP 403 again in this run, so no opened source confirms a flat 13+ rule. Keeping the kids off cloud models stands as a house rule; the wording of the reason stays unverified.

contradictions.what: Family boards. HOM-10 and OCL-03 propose a family board on the Control UI dashboard; the market reviewer rejects the kitchen version (MKT-09) and AUT-10 says no family agent should be given show_widget.
contradictions.resolution: The docs support the cautious side: show_widget needs a Control UI or native client (or a pinned scheduled surface), and any device that can open the board holds operator.read, which includes session reads. The kitchen-tablet versions (HOM-10, MKT-09) are not recommended; the board on the parents' own devices (OCL-03) stays as a later, Tony-only option.

contradictions.what: IPH-04 says pairing plus the phone's permission prompts is all a parent's agent needs to read that phone; the reviewer says the tool itself is owner-only.
contradictions.resolution: The installed source lists nodes, computer and mobile_ui among the core tools that require owner identity, so the reviewer is right: Jordan's agent cannot use the built-in tool and would need an in-house plugin tool.
